extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors submitting papers to the Journal of Integer Sequences (mathematicians working on integer sequences)
extracted.subtask_short: submission to Journal of Integer Sequences
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation expectations for preparing and submitting research papers about integer sequences to the Journal of Integer Sequences, including format, scope, originality, and review process requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission and LaTeX-only format
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic submission is required. Please submit your paper in LaTeX format using a 12pt font. No other formats are currently acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT send pdf, dvi, doc, or docx files of your paper; the journal does not look at them. (You can send pdf files of accompanying figures.) If there are accompanying style files or diagrams, include them. If there are multiple files, send all of them together as a single tar or zip file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use problematic conversion tools or macros
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use tcilatex macros; these result in very poor output. Do not use tools like 'GrindEQ Word-to-LaTeX'; they typically do not produce the high-quality LaTeX that is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal explicitly regrets it cannot handle submissions in Microsoft Word or Word Perfect formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and proofreading requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must be in English and in grammatically correct English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have your paper proofread by a colleague before you submit. If you are not a native English speaker, finding a native speaker to proofread is particularly important. The style guide suggests paid proofreading services. Papers with spelling errors risk being rejected immediately with no possibility for resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the LaTeX style guide and final-version compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: By submitting you agree to follow the guidelines in the journal's LaTeX style guide in the final version of your paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The style guide explains specifics (e.g., how to do accented letters). The final version should conform and may be required in postscript, pdf, dvi, or tex source formats. If you cannot commit the minimal work (generally 2–4 hours) to ensure conformity after acceptance, do not submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify relevance to integer sequences and cite OEIS
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal's main topic is integer sequences; submissions are restricted to papers that deal explicitly with this topic and must justify relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be sure to cite relevant sequences from the OEIS. If you have new sequences, submit them to the OEIS before submission and cite the relevant A-numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of papers sought
rubrics_metrics.description: Desired paper types include: a new integer sequence and its nontrivial interesting properties; new combinatorial interpretations of existing sequences; new mathematically-interesting connections between known sequences; an unexpected appearance of a known sequence; proofs or refutations of conjectures on known sequences; new techniques or algorithms to compute additional terms of hard-to-compute sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your submission fits one of these typical categories or otherwise clearly explains its relevance to integer sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX must compile cleanly (no errors or important warnings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be sure that your submission LaTeX'es properly with no errors or important warning messages. Check the .log files before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are errors or important warnings (such as multiply-defined labels) in the .log file, your paper risks immediate rejection without possibility of resubmission. If you do not know where the .log files are, ask someone to help. If you use TeXworks, remove the --clean option to see the .log file. Reported problems like 'Token not allowed in a PDF string' can be ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove non-ASCII characters from source and bib files
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspect your LaTeX source (and bib files) carefully to remove all non-ASCII characters; these often arise from cutting-and-pasting references from the web.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common problematic characters: wrong minus sign in page ranges, wrong quote marks, wrong apostrophes, and accented letters. Use the style guide for correct accent commands. Do not use UNICODE characters for accents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spell-check and orthography
rubrics_metrics.description: Run your paper through a spell-checker before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers with spelling errors risk being rejected immediately with no possibility for resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject line requirement for email submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject line of your email message should read 'Submission to the Journal of Integer Sequences'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any other header is in danger of being discarded by a spam filter. This is also true for any revision, inquiries about your submission, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include all accompanying files together
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are accompanying style files or diagrams, be sure to include them. If there are multiple files, please send all of them together as a single tar or zip file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids missing files and ensures the editors can compile and view your submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested referees allowed (but not editors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may want to suggest two or three names of possible referees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not suggest members of the editorial board.

rubrics_metrics.name: One submission at a time; no simultaneous submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do not submit additional papers while your current paper is under review. One paper at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By submitting, you certify you have not already published the same paper (or substantially similar) in another journal. Simultaneous submission of the same paper (or substantially similar) to another journal is not permitted. (Preprint archives are fine.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited claims: famous unsolved problems
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal is not accepting any submissions claiming proofs of a list of famous open problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: Goldbach's conjecture; Gilbreath's conjecture; Beal's conjecture; infinitely many twin primes; infinitely many Mersenne primes; Riemann hypothesis; 3x+1 or 'Collatz' problem; Fermat's last theorem; uniqueness of the Markov numbers. Submissions like these will be immediately rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions and rules on use of large language models (LLMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Gemini, or any LLM to write the text (the actual English words) of your paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is permissible to use an LLM to help locate references in the literature (but you must check each suggested reference), and permissible to use an LLM to suggest proof techniques or proofs, but then you must give explicit credit to the LLM within the text of your paper for these suggestions. Use of these AI tools without explicit and detailed delineation of their role will result in immediate rejection and possibly a lifetime ban from the Journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and prior publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should be original, of high quality, and should not have been published in any other journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication on web sites or e-print servers (e.g., arXiv) is explicitly allowed. By publishing in JIS, authors grant the Journal a perpetual, royalty-free license to publish the paper in any collection, while authors retain copyright.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refereeing and review standards
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions will be refereed; the standards are those of any serious mathematical journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers should be worthy of being reviewed by Mathematical Reviews. The editors typically ask referees to complete reports within two months, but in practice reports can take longer; if the editors cannot find willing referees after several months it is likely the paper is not suitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: No page limits; allowance for expository material
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike a traditional journal, there are no page limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should feel free to include as much expository material as they like, provided it adds to the paper and makes it easier to understand. Accompanying documents (computer programs, Maple/Mathematica worksheets, tables) are welcome and will be published alongside the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission contact and timing notes
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions should be sent to the editor-in-chief (Jeffrey O. Shallit) at the provided email and postal address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal does not read e-mail every day. If you do not receive an acknowledgment within fourteen days, then the paper has not been received; do not send inquiries or resubmissions until at least 14 days have passed. During certain periods (e.g., start of school terms, August, late December to early January) there may be no processing of papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative note for authors in China
rubrics_metrics.description: E-mail from many servers in China (such as 163.com) is typically marked as spam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters from China should try submitting from a different e-mail address, such as gmail.com.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fees and warning about scams
rubrics_metrics.description: JIS is completely free for both authors and readers: there are no article processing charges, submission charges, or page charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members of the editorial board receive no remuneration. If you have received an invoice to pay for publication, this is a scam—do not pay it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement on copyright/licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: By publishing in the Journal, authors grant the Journal a perpetual, royalty-free license to publish the paper in any collection of Journal papers in any form; authors retain the copyright of their submitted papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may submit their paper to the arXiv or any other preprint archive at any time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher standard of manuscript preparation expected
rubrics_metrics.description: Therefore, publishing a paper in JIS requires a higher standard of manuscript preparation than many other journals, which have large editorial staff to fix problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are expected to read the style guide carefully and make a real effort to conform. If you cannot commit to the minimal follow-up work after acceptance (2–4 hours), do not submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide bibliographic formatting assistance (BibTeX style)
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal provides a BibTeX style file for preparing bibliographies in BibTeX if authors choose to use it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided style file for consistent bibliography formatting.
